## Content-clock decision and semantic-overlap audit

The last qualifying substantive publication completed at `2026-08-21T16:39:40Z`. Waiting for the next normal daily cycle would breach the rolling 48-hour content target, so a qualifying publication is required today after the product/analytics checks above.

Selected reader question:

> After a coding agent has already worked in a repository, how can I reconstruct the order in which it moved through files, and what conclusions can I safely draw from that replay?

Selected canonical: `/blog/replay-coding-agent-repository-changes/`.

Why this is distinct:

- `/ai-agent-file-access-monitoring/` owns observed file-operation direction and process attribution during a recorded run.
- `/use-cases/review-ai-generated-prs/` owns the code-review decision around a generated patch.
- `/guides/agent-flamegraph/` owns aggregate token/time/operation profiling.
- The new Blog owns post-hoc repository trajectory reconstruction from native local session history: worktree discovery, ordered Tool actions, no-effect frames, media compaction, output artifacts, and the boundary between repository behavior, semantic intent, and independent system observation.
- No existing standalone Agent Nebula or repository-replay article owns that reader decision. The homepage only contains a short product preview.

Primary product sources are pinned to AgentSight v1.0.26 commit `92d634ec02d116a52acae62eb3b9b00c771e0b9d`: the root README, `ext/vis/README.md`, `ext/vis/src/main.rs`, the repository-nebula design contract, and the committed ACTplane Agent Nebula example.

The article intentionally states that `agentsight vis` currently scans local Claude, Codex, and Gemini sessions; it does not generalize that compatibility to every agent supported by other AgentSight surfaces. It also keeps repository replay separate from eBPF/system proof and from semantic explanations of why the agent acted.
